_note: The rules of the layered characters, a first try (docs/art-characters-layers.md), human only. Nothing here is decided: the slots, the names and the colours are a proposal to try. Read by scripts/art/paperdoll.mjs.
_slots: Also the order used when two layers are equally far from the camera, and the stacking order of --how order.
_body: What a slot shows when nothing is worn in it: the race's own body there. This model pack's clothes replace the body under them, so a top takes the place of the bare chest and arms. Bare legs and feet are not rendered yet.

head.model: the base character's head, neck, eyes and brows

bare.model: the base character's chest and arms

ranger.model: Male_Ranger_Body + Arms + Arms_Bracer + Body_Belt_1 + Body_Belt_2 + Acc_Pauldron

_parts: A part may carry "hides": ["hair"]: worn, it empties those slots (a helmet hides hair). "shared": the model is the same for every race (it is still rendered once per race, on that race's hands).
_dressed: Only for the comparison `paperdoll.mjs orders`: the dressed body that parts are cut by when stacking is tried the plain way.
_ramps: The channels a layer pixel can name, in this order (ramps of scripts/art/style.mjs).
_channels: Which of a character's own colours fills each channel when it is drawn: its skin, its hair, the dye of what it wears. null: always the ramp itself.
_colours: The ramps each of those may take. Examples from the ramps that exist today; which colours people, hair and cloth come in is not decided.
